notes: 11 to 8, a 27% cut, inside the contract's 15-35% band. I stopped at 8 rather than forcing 7: the remaining pairs (N3 clearance and N9 the incumbent; N4 two names and N1 the word) have genuinely different option sets, and merging them would have destroyed a decision rather than tidied one. Two corrections to facts the old cards carried: (1) N1 and N11 both said 41 candidate names were 61 — r4-naming-candidates.md:29 reads "41 names, with strategy", and the availability table at :63 is "top 15", so 41 and 15 are the real figures; the wrong number is called out inside the evidence row so it is not quietly restated. (2) N1's problem field cited section 52.3's rank-1 form without a line; it is 22-segments-disclosure-naming.md:219 (`frontmatterapp`), and the prohibition it contradicts is :223, with the falsifier at :225 — all three now cited individually. Every file:line in this file was read with sed before it was written. Three claims from today's briefing were added and are flagged in the prose as coming from the 2026-09-09 round, not from the corpus: the working-tree diff is now free in four editors (weakens the extension route independently of the name), git-backed markdown CMS tools are being weighed as a distribution shelf (which makes Front Matter CMS a shelf neighbour, not only a name neighbour), and nothing in the briefing changes the collision measurements themselves.
